verdict.rationale: Elicit has its own recurring automation: Alerts continuously monitor for new relevant papers and email the user. A newer 'Routine' feature, described on the legacy Alerts page, can act on what it finds by filtering, updating an artifact or writing a summary, which implies recurring agent workflows. However, no evidence shows how a user sets a schedule, cadence or trigger, or how Routines are configured, so only the core monitoring loop is documented. Missing for 10: explicit scheduling/cadence configuration for Routines, dedicated Routine documentation, scheduling of arbitrary workflows (e.g. via API), independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can schedule recurring jobs or workflows

citations.quote: A Routine can act on what it finds and hand you a finished analysis: it can filter on criteria an Alert couldn't, update an artifact, or write the summary
Alerts keep you up to date on the latest research about topics that are relevant to you
Turn on Instant email alerts to be immediately alerted whenever a new relevant research paper is found.
